w:r.w:t: Parse and sort half-hour timestamps; remove duplicate timestamps; retain complete delivery days for fold construction.

Replace infinite values with missing; remove rows missing the target or any required feature. Set only the unavailable initial congestion differences to zero. Optional forecast columns with more than 5% missingness are excluded before locking the feature set.
Fit feature and target scalers on each fold's 90-day training block only; apply unchanged to validation and test data.

Target-day released forecasts and schedules, calendar variables, and realized variables lagged by at least 96 half-hour intervals. Realized target-day price, load, generation, and congestion are excluded.
amazon/chronos-2; context 192; patch length 16; 600 steps; learning rate 1e-5; batch 256; LoRA r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05; q/k/v/o attention and output-patch projection.

PatchTST/TFT/TimeXer: d_model 96, 4 heads, 2 layers, dropout 0.15, batch 32, learning rate 8e-4, at most 160 epochs, patience 20. Transformer: d_model 128, 8 heads, 2 layers; the same budget. DLinear: batch 64, learning rate 1e-3, at most 200 epochs, patience 15.
31 leaves, learning rate 0.05, feature and bagging fractions 0.8, minimum 50 observations per leaf, at most 1,000 rounds, validation patience 50.

Primary registry: at most 1,600 trees; learning rate 0.035; 7 or 15 leaves; minimum child size 30; feature fraction 0.9; row fraction 1.0; L1/L2 penalties 0.05/0.5; patience 60; seed 42. The paired models share the selected absolute- or squared-error objective, temporal weighting with no decay or a 14-day half-life, reference mixture and residual shrinkage of 0.5 or 1.0. The congestion-blind model stops on residual MAE and the expanded model on congestion-weighted trajectory MAE. Table 9 and the stress registry retain their archived 1,200-tree, 0.025-learning-rate, 31-leaf implementation, as specified in their released configurations.

Supply-evidence weights {0.65, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95}; activation thresholds 0.20-0.80 in steps of 0.05; energy thresholds at 41 empirical quantile levels among active calibration observations. Selection follows Section 2.6. Fixed coefficients are 0.50 for the low-price response and 1.0 for the quantile-spread multiplier.

NumPy 1.26.4; pandas 3.0.5; SciPy 1.11.4; scikit-learn 1.7.1; statsmodels 0.14.6; LightGBM 4.6.0; PyTorch 2.11.0; transformers 4.57.6; PEFT 0.19.1; chronos-forecasting 2.3.1; timesfm 2.0.2. These are the versions specified in the released requirements file.
Base model amazon/chronos-2 with a 4.85-MB LoRA adapter; adapter_config.json fixes the base model, PEFT version, target modules, rank, alpha, and dropout. File hashes are supplied in SHA256SUMS.txt.

google/timesfm-2.5-200m-transformers; context 192; 600 adaptation steps; learning rate 1e-4; batch 16; evaluation every 100 steps; LoRA r=4, alpha=8, dropout=0.05 on all linear modules; checkpoint selected by validation loss.

LSTM: hidden width 128, 2 layers, dropout 0.10. CNN-LSTM: 64 filters, kernel 3, LSTM width 128, 2 layers, dropout 0.10. Both use learning rate 1e-3, batch 64, at most 200 epochs, and validation patience 15. CNN-Transformer uses d_model 128, kernel 5, 8 heads, 2 layers, dropout 0.15, learning rate 8e-4, batch 64, at most 220 epochs, and patience 20.

LEAR selects alpha from 100 log-spaced values between 1e-4 and 1e2 by five-fold cross-validation within the training block (maximum 5,000 iterations). Seasonal Naive transfers the matched historical seasonal trajectory and has no fitted hyperparameters.

Retain each fold's Chronos-2 q05, q50 and q95 in CNY/MWh. Define the common shift as the final point forecast minus carrier q50; add it to all three quantiles and project each onto the -200 CNY/MWh floor. The final q50 equals the point forecast. Common-shift widths equal carrier widths before projection; Table C.4 separates the transformation effects.

The ordinary residual baseline adds a full-information LightGBM prediction to the Chronos-2 median, with the same feature set, training/validation periods and two tree-setting candidates; shrinkage is one and early stopping uses residual MAE. Constant-mixture controls reuse the complete model's two fitted residual estimators and reference. Their full-information weights {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} are selected by validation MAE separately for market-floor and nonnegative projections. The residual pair was selected with the routed validation objective. Fold-specific candidates, settings and selected weights accompany the release.

Three 15-day downstream holdouts use preceding 38, 53 or 68 fitting days and seven early-stopping days. The outer carrier, training scalers and label threshold are shared across holdouts. The Wald statistic screens unweighted calibration actions; Eq. (12) reports the weighted diagnostic. The preceding text specifies mapping and test exclusions.
